Today we share these fantastic photos from our last concert at The DiMenna Center, by fine art photographer Tao Ho (@toseiho). 📷

From the night: the players walking on for Brown Leaves Moving, Eric Moe's Laminar Flow, Clara Schumann's Romances, Brahms, and the Schumann Piano Quartet to close, with Guillermo's video running behind the music the whole time.

Thank you to Josefina, Emilie-Anne, Matthew and Julia, and to all of you who came out to start our 12th season with us.

Next up: Winterlight, December 11. ❄️

Thank you, Tao, always so creative!

Petroushka was written for a full orchestra and a ballet company. On December 11 we're playing it with five of us. 🎭

Stravinsky's ballet premiered in Paris in 1911 with the Ballets Russes. It's set at a Shrovetide fair in Russia, where three puppets come to life in a story of love, jealousy and tragedy.

Our chamber arrangement runs about 40 minutes, with projections alongside it, and it closes the evening.

(The image is the first page of the score Stravinsky published in 1911.)

📍 The DiMenna Center, NYC

Sleeping Beauty, Tom Thumb, Beauty and the Beast.

Ravel wrote Ma Mère l'Oye (Mother Goose) for piano four hands between 1908 and 1910, five little pieces built on old French fairy tales.

When we play it at Winterlight, the projections behind us come from illustrations in historical editions of those same stories. The engravings here are Gustave Doré's, for Perrault's Sleeping Beauty.

A project of their own: our directors Guillermo Laporta and Josefina Urraca have put together two free concerts for children and families at Queens libraries. 📚🎶

🎟️ The Queens Passport
Thursday, November 19 · 6–7 PM
Hunters Point Library, 47-40 Center Blvd, Long Island City
Guillermo Laporta and the Ivalas Quartet play classical repertoire and new pieces inspired by the sounds of the neighborhood, and the children help shape the music by conducting guided improvisations. Kids get a passport to stamp and a bilingual English–Spanish activity book.

🎹 The Queens Mother Goose
Saturday, November 21 · 12–1 PM
Flushing Library, 41-17 Main St, Flushing
Pianist Josefina Urraca reimagines Ravel's Mother Goose through the eyes of an immigrant mother raising her child in Queens, with bilingual storytelling and projections inspired by everyday family life. With pianist Yalin Chi and dancer Taylor Hennings. For children ages 2–12 and their families.

Free, no registration needed.

The Queens Passport, a project by Guillermo Laporta, is made possible with funds from the Statewide Community Regrant program, a program of the New York State Council on the Arts with the support of Governor Kathy Hochul and the New York State Legislature and administered by Flushing Town Hall.

The Queens Mother Goose, a project by Josefina Urraca, is made possible (in part) with public funds from the Queens Arts Fund, a re-grant program supported by the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs in partnership with the City Council and administered by New York Foundation for the Arts.

#QueensPublicLibrary #FamilyConcert #Ravel #LongIslandCity #Flushing
